source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Reversal

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side (bull reversal out of a bear trend) only in pseudocode, the book's bear list on pp.108-109 is the exact mirror. Helpers: body(i)=|close[i]-open[i]|; range(i)=high[i]-low[i]; avgBody(n)/avgRange(n)/avgVolume(n) = plain means over bars 1..n; highest(x,n,k)/lowest(x,n,k) = extreme of x over n bars ending k bars ago (k=1 means prior bars only); ema(n); atr(n); tick = instrument minimum move (EL MinMove/PriceScale); bse = ctx.BarsSinceEntry(); overlap(i) = (min(high[i],high[i+1]) - max(low[i],low[i+1])) / range(i).

candidates.name: BullReversalBarShape
candidates.quote: There is a strong bull reversal bar with a large bull trend body and small tails or no tails.
candidates.description: Primitive: the current bar is a strong bull reversal bar - bull close, body at least a fraction of its range, and both tails at most a fraction of its range.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && body(0) >= bodyFraction * range(0) && (high[0] - close[0]) <= tailFraction * range(0) && (open[0] - low[0]) <= tailFraction * range(0)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the reversal bar high
notes: Brooks gives no numbers; 0.6 body and 0.2 tails read 'large body, small tails'.
Used as the signal-bar primitive by most other candidates in this file.

candidates.name: ReversalBarBodyAboveAverage
candidates.quote: a strong bull reversal bar with a large bull trend body
candidates.description: The signal bar's body is large relative to recent bodies: at least K times the average body of the last N bars.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && body(0) >= bodyMultiple * avgBody(lookback)

complexity.reason: window average of bodies over N bars

notes: Splits the 'large' part of sign 1 out of the shape test V02-01.

candidates.name: FollowThroughBullBodies
candidates.quote: The next two or three bars also have bull bodies that are at least the average size of the recent bull and bear bodies.
candidates.description: The bar K bars ago was a bull reversal bar and each of the K bars since (including this one) closed up with a body at least the average body size measured before the reversal bar.
candidates.pseudocode: BullReversalBarShape at [followBars] && forall i in 0..followBars-1: (close[i] > open[i] && body(i) >= avgBody(bodyLookback) measured ending at bar [followBars+1])
candidates.book_order_type: enters at market or on a one- or two-tick pullback once follow-through is seen

complexity.reason: fixed-offset loop plus a window average of bodies

notes: followBars 2..3 per the text.

candidates.name: SpikeWithoutPullback
candidates.quote: The spike grows to five to 10 bars without pulling back for more than a bar or so
candidates.description: Over the last spikeBars bars the market has risen (close[0] > close[spikeBars]) and at most maxPullbackBars bars closed down, with no two consecutive down closes.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > close[spikeBars] && countif(i in 0..spikeBars-1, close[i] < open[i]) <= maxPullbackBars && no i in 0..spikeBars-2 with (close[i] < open[i] && close[i+1] < open[i+1])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (strength assessment; Brooks adds on pullbacks during the spike)

complexity.reason: window loop counting down bars over N bars

notes: spikeBars grid 5..10.

candidates.name: SpikeReversesPriorSwingHighs
candidates.quote: it reverses many bars, swing highs, and bear flags of the prior bear trend.
candidates.description: The spike has closed above at least K of the swing-high pivots formed during the prior bear trend within the lookback.
candidates.pseudocode: count of swing-high pivots p (strength s) within lookback with close[0] > high[p] >= minSwingHighsReversed

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection over a variable window

notes: The bar-count form (close above N prior highs) is V02-33; this is the pivot form.

candidates.name: LowHoldsPriorClose
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike have a low that is at or just one tick below the close of the prior bar.
candidates.description: This bar's low is no more than T ticks below the previous bar's close - buyers did not let the prior close be tested.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] >= close[1] - toleranceTicks * tick
notes: Tick size must come from the instrument; the parameter is in ticks.

candidates.name: OpenAbovePriorClose
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike have an open that is above the close of the prior bar.
candidates.description: This bar opened above the previous bar's close (a small gap up at the open).
candidates.pseudocode: open[0] > close[1]

candidates.name: CloseOnHigh
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike have a close on the high of the bar or just one tick below its high.
candidates.description: This bar closed within T ticks of its high.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] - close[0] <= toleranceTicks * tick
notes: CloseRangePosition is the fractional form; this is the absolute-ticks form.

candidates.name: SpikeBarQualityCount
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike have a low that is at or just one tick below the close of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Within the last spikeBars bars, at least K bars show one of the spike-quality features (low holds prior close, open above prior close, close on high).
candidates.pseudocode: countif(i in 0..spikeBars-1, LowHoldsPriorClose[i] || OpenAbovePriorClose[i] || CloseOnHigh[i]) >= minQualityBars
notes: Brooks says 'one or more'; the count form makes the strength tunable.

candidates.name: BearTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: after a strong break above the bear trend line.
candidates.description: Primitive: the close is above the bear trend line projected through the two most recent swing highs of the prior bear trend.
candidates.pseudocode: line = projectLine(swingHigh[2], swingHigh[1]) to bar 0; close[0] > line + marginTicks * tick

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a trend-line projection

notes: Defined here as this file's trend-line primitive; other chapters define the same thing.

candidates.name: TestOfBearLowAfterTrendLineBreak
candidates.quote: The overall context makes a reversal likely, like a higher low or lower low test of the bear low after a strong break above the bear trend line.
candidates.description: A bear trend line break occurred within the last N bars; price has since returned to within a tolerance of the bear low (higher low, double bottom, or lower low) and a bull reversal bar forms.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSince(BearTrendLineBreak) <= breakLookback && abs(low[0] - bearLow) <= testTolerance * atr(atrLen) && BullReversalBarShape[0]  where bearLow = lowest(low, breakLookback, 1)
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: depends on the trend-line primitive and cross-bar state for the break

notes: This is the 'major trend reversal' context; the same composite is defined in ch.01 and Part I.

candidates.name: BreakoutBarClosesAboveManyPriorHighs
candidates.quote: The first or second bar of the breakout has a close that is above the highs of many prior bars.
candidates.description: This bar (or the prior bar) closes above the highest high of the N bars before it.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > highest(high, priorBars, 1) || close[1] > highest(high, priorBars, 2)
notes: The 'first or second bar' wording is the OR of offsets 0 and 1.

candidates.name: FirstPullbackOnlyAfterMinBars
candidates.quote: The first pullback occurs only after three or more bars.
candidates.description: Buy the first pullback bar: this bar is the first down-close since a bull reversal bar k bars ago and k-1 >= minBars up closes came between.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] < open[0] && exists k >= minBars+1 with BullReversalBarShape[k] && forall i in 1..k-1: close[i] > open[i]
candidates.book_order_type: buy on a stop above the pullback bar (mechanized: pullback bar close then next open)

complexity.reason: counter of bars since a pattern bar persists across bars

candidates.name: ShortPullbackResumption
candidates.quote: The first pullback lasts only one or two bars
candidates.description: After a run of up closes, the pullback was at most maxPullbackBars down closes and this bar closes back above the pullback's high.
candidates.pseudocode: k = count of consecutive down closes ending at bar 1; 1 <= k <= maxPullbackBars && close[0] > highest(high, k, 1) && close[k+1] > open[k+1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the pullback high

complexity.reason: short backward loop over a variable but bounded number of bars

candidates.name: PullbackNotAfterStrongBearReversalBar
candidates.quote: it follows a bar that is not a strong bear reversal bar.
candidates.description: Filter: the bar that started the pullback (the last up-close bar before it) was not a strong bear reversal bar - i.e. the mirror of V02-01 with a high above the prior high did not occur at the pullback's start.
candidates.pseudocode: k = count of consecutive down closes ending at bar 1; !(BearReversalBarShape[k] && high[k] > high[k+1])   // BearReversalBarShape is V02-01 mirrored

complexity.reason: bounded backward loop plus single-bar shape test

notes: Negation of a shape test; pairs with V02-14.

candidates.name: BreakevenStop
candidates.quote: The first pullback does not hit a breakeven stop (the entry price).
candidates.description: Once open profit has reached an activation level, exit if the bar trades back to the entry price (breakeven stop). Brooks's sign: a strong reversal never hits this stop.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() > 0 && ctx.MaxPositionProfit() >= activationDollars && low[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice()

complexity.reason: position-history read (peak profit) and entry price

notes: Activation could alternatively be 'first follow-through trend bar' rather than dollars.

candidates.name: CloseAboveEmaByMargin
candidates.quote: The spike goes very far and breaks several resistance levels like the moving average, prior swing highs, and trend lines, and each by many ticks.
candidates.description: The close is above the N-bar EMA by at least a margin (in ticks).
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > ema(emaLen) + marginTicks * tick
notes: CloseAboveAverage has no margin and uses a simple average.

candidates.name: CloseAbovePriorSwingHighByMargin
candidates.quote: breaks several resistance levels like the moving average, prior swing highs, and trend lines, and each by many ticks.
candidates.description: The close is above the most recent swing-high pivot by at least a margin in ticks.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > lastSwingHigh(pivotStrength) + marginTicks * tick
notes: The N-bar-highest proxy is CloseAbovePriorHighestHigh with a margin.

candidates.name: TrendLineBreakByMargin
candidates.quote: breaks several resistance levels like ... trend lines, and each by many ticks.
candidates.description: The bear trend line break (V02-10) is by at least a margin of ticks - a strong rather than marginal break.
candidates.pseudocode: BearTrendLineBreak with marginTicks = strongMarginTicks
notes: Parameterization of V02-10; kept separate because Brooks treats 'by many ticks' as its own sign.

candidates.name: SecondReversalSignal
candidates.quote: The signal is the second attempt to reverse within the past few bars (a second signal).
candidates.description: This bar is a bull reversal bar and another bull reversal bar formed 2..N bars ago whose high was not followed through (some later bar closed below its low).
candidates.pseudocode: BullReversalBarShape[0] && exists k in 2..windowBars with BullReversalBarShape[k] && lowest(low, k-1, 1) < low[k]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the second signal bar

complexity.reason: cross-bar state: remembering an earlier signal bar and whether it failed

notes: 'Failed' is read as the first signal's low being broken before the second forms.

candidates.name: TrendChannelLineOvershootReversal
candidates.quote: The reversal began as a reversal from an overshoot of a trend channel line from the old trend.
candidates.description: Price poked below the bear trend channel line (parallel of the bear trend line anchored at the lows) within the last K bars and this bar closes back above it.
candidates.pseudocode: tcl = parallel of bear trend line through swingLow[1]; lowest(low, overshootBars, 0) < tcl && close[0] > tcl
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: needs pivots, a trend line and a parallel channel projection

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutBelowSwingLow
candidates.quote: It is reversing a significant swing high or low (e.g., it breaks below a strong prior swing low and reverses up).
candidates.description: This bar traded below the lowest low of the prior N bars and closed back above it with a bull body.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < lowest(low, lookback, 1) && close[0] > lowest(low, lookback, 1) && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar
notes: N-bar-low proxy for 'significant swing low'; the pivot form would be hard.

candidates.name: PullbackSignalBarIsReversalBar
candidates.quote: The high 1 and high 2 pullbacks have strong bull reversal bars for signal bars.
candidates.description: In the new bull leg, the bar that ends a pullback (first bar whose high exceeds the prior bar's high after >=1 down closes) is itself a strong bull reversal bar.
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && high[0] > high[1] && BullReversalBarShape[0] && close[0] > close[pullbackLookback]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the H1/H2 signal bar

complexity.reason: H1/H2 leg counting is hard; this is the first-leg proxy without the count

notes: Full high-1/high-2 counting would raise this to hard; recorded as the H1 proxy.

candidates.name: TrendingCloses
candidates.quote: It has trending 'anything': closes, highs, lows, or bodies.
candidates.description: Each of the last N closes is above the close before it.
candidates.pseudocode: forall i in 0..trendBars-1: close[i] > close[i+1]
notes: ConsecutiveCloseExit is the exit form; ConsecutiveUpBars tests close vs open, not close vs prior close.

candidates.name: TrendingHighsAndLows
candidates.quote: It has trending 'anything': closes, highs, lows, or bodies.
candidates.description: Each of the last N bars has a higher high and a higher low than the bar before it.
candidates.pseudocode: forall i in 0..trendBars-1: high[i] > high[i+1] && low[i] > low[i+1]
notes: Could be split into highs-only and lows-only; the authoring pass can choose.

candidates.name: TrendingBodies
candidates.quote: It has trending 'anything': closes, highs, lows, or bodies.
candidates.description: Each of the last N bars has a body top and body bottom above those of the bar before it.
candidates.pseudocode: forall i in 0..trendBars-1: max(open[i],close[i]) > max(open[i+1],close[i+1]) && min(open[i],close[i]) > min(open[i+1],close[i+1])

candidates.name: SmallSidewaysPullbacks
candidates.quote: The pullbacks are small and sideways.
candidates.description: The deepest pullback inside the last N bars retraced no more than a fraction of the N-bar advance.
candidates.pseudocode: adv = highest(high, lookback, 0) - lowest(low, lookback, 0); maxPullback = max over i in 0..lookback-1 of (highest(high, lookback-i, i) - low[i]) restricted to bars after the low; maxPullback <= pullbackFraction * adv

complexity.reason: nested window loop tracking a running high and the deepest dip from it

notes: Equivalent to a max-drawdown over the window relative to the window range.

candidates.name: PriorTrendLineBreaks
candidates.quote: There were prior breaks of earlier bear trend lines (this isn't the first sign of bullish strength).
candidates.description: Filter: at least K distinct bear-trend-line breaks have occurred within the lookback before the current signal.
candidates.pseudocode: count of BearTrendLineBreak events (each against the then-current line) in bars 1..lookback >= minPriorBreaks

complexity.reason: requires re-drawing trend lines as pivots evolve and counting break events

candidates.name: PullbackOverlappingBars
candidates.quote: The pullback to test the bear low lacks momentum, as evidenced by its having many overlapping bars
candidates.description: Over the last N bars of a down move, the average overlap between adjacent bars is at least a fraction of bar range - a low-momentum pullback worth buying.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] < close[pullbackBars] && average over i in 0..pullbackBars-1 of overlap(i) >= minOverlap
notes: Sides: for the long side the pullback is a down move; mirror for shorts.

candidates.name: PullbackBullBarFraction
candidates.quote: many overlapping bars with many being bull trend bars.
candidates.description: Over the last N bars of a down move, at least a fraction of the bars have bull bodies - the sellers lack conviction.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] < close[pullbackBars] && countif(i in 0..pullbackBars-1, close[i] > open[i]) >= bullFraction * pullbackBars

candidates.name: PullbackHoldsAboveEma
candidates.quote: The pullback that tests the bear low fails at the moving average or the old bear trend line.
candidates.description: The pullback's lowest low over the last N bars stayed at or above the EMA (within a tolerance) and this bar closes up - the moving average held as support.
candidates.pseudocode: lowest(low, pullbackBars, 0) >= ema(emaLen) - toleranceTicks * tick && close[0] > open[0] && close[1] < close[pullbackBars]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the bar that holds the average

candidates.name: PullbackHoldsAboveOldTrendLine
candidates.quote: fails at the moving average or the old bear trend line.
candidates.description: After the bear trend line was broken, the pullback's lowest low stays at or above the projected old bear trend line and this bar closes up.
candidates.pseudocode: lowest(low, pullbackBars, 0) >= bearTrendLineValue[0] - toleranceTicks * tick && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the bar that holds the line
notes: The broken resistance line becoming support (a breakout test).

candidates.name: BarsReversedByClose
candidates.quote: this breakout bar has a high and close that are above the highs and closes of five or even 20 or more bars.
candidates.description: The close is above the highs of at least N consecutive prior bars (the number of bars 'reversed' by the close).
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > highest(high, barsReversed, 1)
notes: Grid 5..20 per the text; Brooks says close-based reversal is stronger than high-based (V02-34).

candidates.name: BarsReversedByHigh
candidates.quote: A large number of bars reversed by the close of the bull bar is a stronger sign than a similar number of bars reversed by only its high.
candidates.description: The high is above the highs of at least N consecutive prior bars - the weaker, high-based form of V02-33.
candidates.pseudocode: high[0] > highest(high, barsReversed, 1) && close[0] > open[0]

candidates.name: NoCountertrendInStrongTrendWithoutBreak
candidates.quote: When there is a strong trend, traders should not be taking countertrend trades until there has been a trend line break or at least a climactic reversal from a trend channel line overshoot.
candidates.description: Filter: a long against a bear trend is allowed only if a bear trend line break or a trend-channel-line overshoot reversal has occurred within the lookback.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSince(BearTrendLineBreak) <= lookback || barsSince(TrendChannelLineOvershootReversal) <= lookback

complexity.reason: both components need pivots and line projection

notes: The single most repeated rule of the trilogy; expect it in every reversals chapter.

candidates.name: TradingRangeAllowsBothDirections
candidates.quote: In a trading range market, however, traders can trade reversals in both directions.
candidates.description: Filter: the market is in a trading range (e.g. N-bar range small relative to ATR, or EMA flat), so reversal entries need no prior trend line break.
candidates.pseudocode: (highest(high, lookback, 0) - lowest(low, lookback, 0)) <= rangeAtrMultiple * atr(atrLen)

complexity.reason: 'the market is in a trading range' needs a design decision; the ATR-range proxy is one option

notes: ADX-below-threshold is an existing proxy for the same regime.

candidates.name: TradingRangeBottomBuyWithoutSignalBar
candidates.quote: If instead the market is simply rallying to the top of a trading range, they may not even need a reversal bar when they are shorting.
candidates.description: In a trading range, buy when the close is in the bottom fraction of the N-bar range, with no reversal-bar requirement (mirror: short at the top).
candidates.pseudocode: (close[0] - lowest(low, lookback, 0)) / (highest(high, lookback, 0) - lowest(low, lookback, 0)) <= bottomFraction
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the range extreme or stop above any bar
notes: Gate with V02-36 in a composite; standalone it fades every strong trend.

candidates.name: WedgeBullFlagBuyAboveBearBar
candidates.quote: if the market is in a wedge bull flag and they are looking for it to reverse back up into the bull trend, they might even be willing to buy above a bear trend bar.
candidates.description: In a bull trend, after three pushes down (wedge bull flag), buy when the close exceeds the high of the prior bar even if that prior bar was a bear trend bar.
candidates.pseudocode: bullTrendContext && threePushesDown(pivotStrength) && close[0] > high[1]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the bear trend bar

complexity.reason: three-push (wedge) recognition needs pivots and leg counting

notes: The point Brooks makes is that the signal-bar requirement relaxes with context.

candidates.name: ReversalStrengthScore
candidates.quote: There are many characteristics of strong reversals, and the more that are present, the more likely a countertrend trade will be profitable
candidates.description: Composite score: the number of mechanizable signs of strength present on this bar is at least K.
candidates.pseudocode: score = sum of booleans of the composed candidates evaluated at bar 0; score >= minSigns
candidates.book_order_type: enter at market or on a small pullback once enough signs are present

complexity.reason: sum of simple tests; the EMA member makes it moderate

notes: Only the trivial/simple/moderate signs are composed; the hard ones can be added once authored.

rejected.quote: As the first bar of the reversal is forming, it spends most of its time near its high and the pullbacks are less than a quarter of the height of the growing bar.
rejected.reason: needs tick-level data inside the bar

rejected.quote: There is a sense of urgency. You feel like you have to buy but you want a pullback, yet it never comes.
rejected.reason: pure discretion; the mechanizable part is already V02-04

rejected.quote: if the market is a zero-sum game, how can it have 95 percent of the participants be profitable institutions?

chapter_summary: A two-page checklist of what a strong bull (and, mirrored, bear) reversal looks like. Each sign was mined as its own candidate: single-bar spike-quality tests (close on high, open above prior close, low holds prior close, reversal-bar shape), window tests (follow-through bodies, spike without pullback, bars reversed by close/high, trending closes/highs/lows/bodies, pullback overlap and bull-bar fraction), EMA tests (close above EMA by margin, pullback holds EMA), a breakeven-stop exit, and hard context items (trend line break, trend channel overshoot, swing highs reversed, prior line breaks). A composite strength score closes the file. The mirror list on pp.108-109 adds nothing new.
